did_you_know.text: Did you know? Elisha warned the Shunammite woman about a famine that would last seven years and told her to leave the country with her household.
Did you know? The Shunammite woman did exactly as Elisha said and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
Did you know? After she returned to the country, the king ordered that the Shunammite woman’s house, field, and all the produce that had accumulated since she left be restored to her.
Did you know? Hazael came to Elisha carrying a gift consisting of all the finest goods of Damascus—a load carried by forty camels.
Did you know? Elisha gave Hazael a twofold message: Ben-hadad would recover from his illness, but the LORD had revealed to him that Ben-hadad would certainly die.
Did you know? Elisha wept because he knew that Hazael would inflict terrible and cruel acts of war on the Israelites.
Did you know? The next day, Hazael told Ben-hadad that Elisha had said he would recover, but the account describes how Ben-hadad died and Hazael succeeded him as king.

Did you know? Although Jehoram king of Judah did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, the LORD did not destroy Judah, because of his promise to David to give him and his descendants a lamp—that is, to preserve the Davidic dynasty.
Did you know? During Jehoram’s reign, Edom rebelled against Judah and appointed a king of its own; as a result, Judah lost direct control over Edom.
Did you know? Ahaziah king of Judah reigned in Jerusalem for only one year, and his mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
